intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Hoxha-Aliu syndrome (HXAL) is caused by homozygous or other biallelic null mutation in the ERI1 gene on chromosome 8p23.

checks.claim: Hoxha-Aliu syndrome (HXAL) is caused by homozygous or other biallelic null mutation in the ERI1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we present a case of a female patient with a homozygous nonsense variant in ERI1 gene.
checks.explanation: The paper reports a single homozygous nonsense (null) variant. It does not address other biallelic genotypes.

checks.claim: The ERI1 gene is located on chromosome 8p23.

paragraphs.text: Hoxha-Aliu syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder associated with biallelic null variants in the ERI1 gene, which encodes a 3-prime-to-5-prime exoribonuclease. Affected individuals show mild intellectual disability or developmental delay and digital anomalies of the hands and feet, such as brachydactyly, clinodactyly, short nails of the halluces, short metacarpals, and toe syndactyly (Hoxha and Aliu, 2023; Guo et al., 2023).

checks.explanation: The title describes the condition as autosomal recessive.

checks.claim: Hoxha-Aliu syndrome is associated with biallelic null variants in the ERI1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Here, we present a case of a female patient with a homozygous nonsense variant in ERI1 gene.
checks.explanation: The paper shows only one homozygous nonsense variant, not biallelic null variants in general.

checks.claim: The ERI1 gene encodes a 3-prime-to-5-prime exoribonuclease.
checks.evidence_quote: ERI1 is an evolutionary conserved 3'-5' exonuclease with an important function in multiple RNA processing pathways.
checks.explanation: The paper describes ERI1 as a 3'-5' exonuclease acting in RNA processing, which matches an exoribonuclease.

paragraphs.text: Szot et al. (2021) reported a girl (F5.II.1) who was homozygous for a missense variant in the KYNU gene and was considered to have congenital NAD deficiency disorder; she was also homozygous for a nonsense variant in ERI1 (see MOLECULAR GENETICS). Her features included a perimembranous ventricular septal defect, pulmonary vein stenosis, and limb reduction defects (right hand transverse terminal limb reduction with a rudimentary fifth digit, hypoplastic deep-set or absent nails, absent toes, and syndactyly), as well as microcephaly, global developmental delay, autism, craniofacial dysmorphism, and bilateral inguinal hernias. Szot et al. (2021) noted that the ERI1 variant might confound the contribution of mild NAD deficiency to her phenotype.

paragraphs.text: Guo et al. (2023) identified biallelic ERI1 variants in 8 affected individuals from 7 unrelated families. Individuals with biallelic null variants showed mild intellectual disability and digital anomalies, whereas 5 individuals with missense variants had severe SEMD. The missense variants caused loss of exoribonuclease activity, resulting in defective trimming of the 3-prime end of 5.8S rRNA and decreased degradation of replication-dependent histone mRNAs. Induced pluripotent stem cells derived from affected individuals showed impaired in vitro chondrogenesis with downregulation of genes regulating skeletal patterning.

The patient was also homozygous for a glu206-to-lys (E206K) variant in the KYNU gene, and the authors noted that the ERI1 variant might confound the contribution of mild NAD deficiency to her phenotype.

agent.process_note: I read all 4 papers. Three of them (Choucair 2017, Hoxha and Aliu 2023, Guo 2023) were available only as abstracts. Szot 2021 was full text; I read all of it and searched it for 'ERI1' and 'consanguin'. The ERI1 finding in Szot is incidental: their patient F5.II.1 was also homozygous for a KYNU missense variant. Not found: the exact nonsense variant in Hoxha and Aliu (the abstract does not give it); the specific variants, zygosity patterns, ancestry and consanguinity of Guo's families; and consanguinity for Szot's F5.II.1. No gene MIM number was supplied, so none is given. The chromosome location (8p23) comes from the 8p23.1 deletion described by Choucair et al. Hoxha and Aliu's patient and Szot's F5.II.1 are both female and homozygous for a nonsense variant, but I have not assumed they are the same person. The SEMD seen with missense variants (Guo) is covered only in the genotype-phenotype section.
